**Finding submitted: deviation (IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data), confidence 0.82.**

What I found in Section 7.0 Materials (paragraphs p0082–p0086):

1. **Wrong-way default (p0082):** undesignated Materials default to **Type II**, i.e. IBM/third-party owned — so anything IBM omits to label becomes IBM's property even though we funded it.
2. **Thin licence back (p0085):** for Type II Materials we get only use/reproduce/display/perform/distribute "**within Customer's Enterprise only**" — no right to modify, create derivatives or sublicense, which fails both the preferred and fallback positions.
3. **Over-broad grant of our IP (p0084):** on Materials we *do* own, IBM gets an irrevocable, worldwide, paid-up licence to distribute **externally** and to **authorise others** to do the same — functionally letting IBM exploit and hand on our work product.
4. **No Customer Data ownership statement:** §11.6 only makes us *responsible* for Content, §14.18 covers contact data, and §14.17 grants only express licences — nothing affirms our ownership of Content, Customer Components or data, and nothing bars joint ownership.

Redline (validated, ok:true): default flipped to Type I; IBM's licence in Customer-owned Materials narrowed to internal use and Subcontractors solely to perform the Services; Type II licence upgraded to perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free with modify/derivative/sublicense rights for our business; new clause (e) confirming Customer retains all right, title and interest in Content and Customer Components, no assignment to IBM, and no joint ownership. Fallback offered in the comment (IBM keeps generic tools/know-how) provided the licence-back and data-ownership language survives.
